body: ActRaiser 2 is a Super Nintendo action platformer that sends the Master into lands suffering under demonic influence. A floating palace provides the view over the world, and the player descends to confront the forces responsible for each region's plight. The sequel concentrates on the fighting and movement that formed one half of the original game. A winged body changes those encounters, allowing the player to glide and negotiate more elaborate arrangements of enemies and platforms while choosing when to strike with the sword.

Magic is prepared by charging an attack and released in a form determined by the Master's position. Standing, jumping or using another posture can therefore change the tool available against an enemy. Limited scrolls make the decision worth considering before a difficult encounter. Wings provide further control in the air, while a shield can turn aside some incoming attacks. The challenge depends on learning how those abilities fit together, because a safe landing and a useful attack often have to be prepared as part of the same movement.

The regions draw on the seven deadly sins, with their inhabitants' troubles supplying the reason to enter the next dangerous area. Two acts develop each location's conflict before the campaign moves onward. Yuzo Koshiro returned to compose the score, supporting the sequel's more solemn visual character. Released in Japan in 1993, the game places greater demands on precise movement and the use of magic. Its change of emphasis gives the series a different identity, built around mastering the physical abilities of the figure descending from the palace.
story_headings: A more concentrated kind of journey
